description:
We are participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 focusing on the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge.

We are looking for passionate teammates with skills in:

 * Data Analysis & Earth Science

 * Coding & Software Development

 * Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning

 * Data Visualization

Join us if you are excited about processing satellite data and building impactful environmental solutions!
summary:
FIRECHRONICLE is a satellite-based fire intelligence platform designed to harmonize and visualize active fire detections from NASA’s MODIS and VIIRS satellite sensors. It brings satellite observations together in an interactive 3D Earth environment and a historical Burning Activity Calendar, helping users explore fire activity across different locations and time periods.
The project addresses the challenge of making satellite fire observations easier to understand, compare, and monitor. By organizing data from multiple sensors into one platform, FIRECHRONICLE aims to help researchers, environmental organizations, land managers, and emergency responders identify patterns, monitor changes in fire activity, and prioritize areas that may require attention.
FIRECHRONICLE is important because timely access to understandable satellite information can support better environmental monitoring, research, and preparedness. It transforms complex satellite observations into a more accessible and meaningful view of fire activity worldwide.
details:
FIRECHRONICLE is a web-based satellite fire intelligence platform. It helps users explore, monitor and analyze fire activity more easily. The platform combines NASA MODIS and VIIRS data on fires and thermal anomalies. It uses a 3D Earth view and a set of specialized tools to make the data more useful.

One of the features is the Global Overview. This allows users to look at fire activity around the world. The Fire Explorer lets users filter results by day or night observations, confidence levels and Fire Radiative Power (FRP). There are ways to view the data, including 3D Flames, Activity Columns, Heat Density and Clusters.

The Historical Analysis section shows trends over time. Users can see weekly, monthly and seasonal patterns. There is also a -year Burning Activity Calendar. This section includes country-level anomaly detection to highlight fire activity.

The Early Warning section helps identify areas that need attention. It ranks monitoring priorities based on activity how long the activity has lasted and how much it differs from what is normal over the years. The Country Intelligence feature lets users dive into fire data by country.

FIRECHRONICLE is designed to help researchers, environmental groups, land managers and emergency response teams. Its goal is to make satellite data easier to understand. The platform aims to boost awareness support scientific research and help decide where to focus monitoring and investigation.

The project was built as a web application using Lovable. It uses NASA FIRMS data. Includes 3D geographical visualization. The approach combines exploration, different visualization styles, historical trends and priority assessment, in one single platform.

During development the team focused on reliability, sensor differences, geographic accuracy, data availability and ease of use. They also made sure to distinguish between anomalies and confirmed fires. FIRECHRONICLE does not treat satellite detections as proof of a wildfire. It is meant to support decision-making not to replace ground verification.
